text.title: Writing Design Documents Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding Writing Design Documents: AD-X format and coverage, document hierarchy and when to write, and the explicit-types/contracts/references pattern for LLM code generation. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override.

section.title: Background
section.p: Rules r-design-after-spec-before-plan through r-ad-x-six-fields cover the document hierarchy in SDD, when to write a design doc, SDD-optimized structure, AD-X decision format, and Y-statement concise form. Rule r-explicit-types-contracts-refs covers the four patterns for structuring design docs to enable reliable LLM code generation: explicit file patterns, type definitions, API contracts, and reference tables. Comparison of RFC/TDD/ADR/mini doc types. The four patterns are worked in content/05-examples.xml.

list.item: constitution.md: project-wide tech decisions and standards
spec.md: FR-X requirements and AC-X acceptance criteria (WHAT/WHY)
design.md: AD-X architectural decisions, file structure, data models, API contracts (HOW)
implementation-plan.md: waves, task breakdown, token estimates (ORDER)
TASK-XXX-*.md: executable tasks (EXECUTE)

section.p: When to write a design doc:

list.item: Required: 5+ files touched, DB schema change, API contract modification, cross-service dependency, security-sensitive change
Optional: refactoring with no interface changes (maybe if architecture changes)
Skip: bug fix 1-2 files, small feature 1-2 files no arch impact, single task under ~5k tokens, greenfield spike
Reference Documents: links to spec, constitution, related designs
Spec Coverage: FR-X to AD-X traceability matrix
Architectural Decisions: AD-X blocks with rationale and alternatives
File Structure: exact files to create/modify with patterns
Data Models: database schemas, TypeScript types, Pydantic models
API Contracts: endpoints with request/response/error examples
Dependencies: packages and external services
Security Considerations: auth, validation, encryption
Performance Considerations: caching, optimization, scaling
Testing Strategy: unit, integration, E2E approach

section.p: Y-statement concise form: "In the context of [use case], facing [concern], we decided for [option] to achieve [quality], accepting [downside]."

list.item: RFC (Request for Comments): proposing changes needing team consensus; sections: summary, motivation, proposal, drawbacks, alternatives, implementation; used by Stripe, HashiCorp, Uber
TDD (Technical Design Document): detailed technical specification for complex systems; 10+ sections including architecture, data model, API, security, reliability, monitoring
ADR (Architecture Decision Record): recording a single architectural decision; sections: context, decision, consequences; lightweight, append-only
SDD Design Doc: LLM-optimized full feature design with AD-X traceability matrix; the primary format for SDD workflow
Lightweight/Mini: 1-2 page doc for small changes; overview, decision, files changed

section.reference: Prompts for drafting and reviewing design docs
Shell script checking AD-X blocks for required fields

rule.statement: Every architectural decision has an AD-X id and lists alternative, tradeoff, chosen-option, traced-requirement.
rule.rationale: Every architectural decision has an AD-X id and lists alternative, tradeoff, chosen-option, traced-requirement.

rule.statement: Every FR-X from spec.md is covered by at least one AD-X or named subsystem.
rule.rationale: Every FR-X from spec.md is covered by at least one AD-X or named subsystem.

rule.statement: Every API contract has example request, example response, and an error matrix.
rule.rationale: Every API contract has example request, example response, and an error matrix.

rule.statement: design.md does not restate the spec; it references FR-X ids and answers HOW.
rule.rationale: design.md does not restate the spec; it references FR-X ids and answers HOW.

rule.statement: design.md carries semver version + last_reviewed; bumped when AD set changes.
rule.rationale: design.md carries semver version + last_reviewed; bumped when AD set changes.

rule.statement: Write design.md after spec.md is approved and before writing implementation-plan.md; never skip this order.
rule.rationale: The spec defines intent (WHAT/WHY); the design defines mechanism (HOW); the implementation plan defines sequence (WHEN/ORDER). Reversing the order produces implementations without explicit decision records and specs without feasibility validation.

rule.statement: Write a design doc when a feature touches 5+ files, changes a DB schema, modifies an API contract, introduces cross-service dependencies, or has security implications.
rule.rationale: Design docs prevent the most expensive failure modes: incompatible implementations from parallel agents, undocumented architectural decisions re-litigated later, and security issues discovered post-implementation.

rule.statement: Every AD-X must have: Status, Context, Decision, Rationale, Alternatives Considered table, and Consequences; mark Status as Proposed until human-approved.
rule.rationale: Agents must not implement Proposed decisions. The Alternatives Considered table prevents the decision from becoming pseudo-documentation — without it, the document records a conclusion without reasoning.

rule.statement: Include explicit type definitions, concrete API contracts with error codes, and reference tables pointing to existing code patterns — do not rely on prose descriptions alone.
rule.rationale: LLMs generate more accurate code from explicit types than from prose. API contracts without concrete error examples lead to incompatible implementations. File references allow agents to read existing patterns instead of inventing new ones.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-writing-design-documents.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.
